content:
maria: Nightly eval spike on prompt_set_3 — lots of short completions with repeated rare-token bursts, quality down across several prompts :eyes:
nightly-bot: Nightly job 2024-04-12 03:12 UTC: eval/regressions/prompt_set_3 failure rate increased 18% -> 31%. Full report: https://redwood.internal/evals/2024-04-12/ps3 (summary attached)
tom: Yep, I saw the report. This started right after the kernel reorder PR landed last night (commit abcdef1). Could be KV prefetch ordering interacting with sampler.
priya: Quick local run (q4f build, quantized) reproduced. Deterministic seed shows odd mid-gen bursts of rare glyphs. Example fragment: "the model returns ▁∑∑∑ ∑∑ error and then continues" — you can see the rare tokens cluster in the middle rather than at the start.
zack: Can you paste a minimal repro and the flags you used? I want to isolate RNG vs cache ordering.
priya: Repro snippet:
```python
# run against local inference: deterministic sampling
from redwood import Client
c = Client(url="http://localhost:8080")
resp = c.generate(model="gptx-6b-q4f", prompt="Explain recursion in simple terms", max_tokens=120, top_k=50, top_p=0.95, temperature=0.8, seed=42)
print(resp.text)
```
Output (truncated):
"... recursion is when a function calls itself ▁∑∑∑ ∑∑ then it returns the base case ..."
Note the weird cluster after ~40 tokens.
maria: Nightly diffs: the reorder changed contiguous KV reads from N->M to M->N and introduced async prefetch overlap. If sampler reads logits during a partial prefetch, normalization may be off.
sre-bot: Deploy record: commit abcdef1 applied to inference-prod at 2024-04-12T02:58Z (triggered by CI deploy pipeline).
tom: I did a quick bisect. Setting REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_ORDER=old locally reverts the behavior (no bursts). With the new order we consistently see token-burst spikes for the same seeds. Hypothesis: prefetch advances kvcache pointers ahead of when sampler consumes logits -> sampler operates on stale/shifted KV alignment.
priya: Logs showing interleaving (timestamps are ms):
```
[02:57:54.128] kvcache_prefetch: range start=1024 end=2048 request_id=0x7f
[02:57:54.130] sampler_read_logits: seq=512 request_id=0x7f
[02:57:54.131] kvcache_apply: apply_idx=1536 request_id=0x7f
[02:57:54.132] sampler_compute_probs: seq=512 request_id=0x7f
```
You can see sampler_read_logits happens prior to the prefetch apply but after the prefetch request -> partial state.
zack: I reproduced end-to-end. Ran the nightly eval harness on staging with REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_ORDER=old and failure rate dropped back to baseline (31% -> 19%). Re-ran with commit abcdef1 and saw 30% again.
maria: Action options: 1) Rollback the reorder in prod ASAP, 2) Add a read-after-prefetch barrier in sampler, 3) Harden with integration tests.
tom: I'll open a rollback PR and also a follow-up patch that adds a simple memory barrier and a unit test that exercises deterministic seeds across both orders. PRs: rollback #482, sampler-barrier #483.
priya: Also adding an integration test in nightly that compares per-seed entropy and token distributions between control and candidate builds (alert on >5% per-prompt entropy shift).
deploy-bot: PR #482 (revert kernel reorder) merged to canary at 2024-04-12T04:10Z. Canary run: 20/20 prompt_set_3 samples passed. Rolling to prod in 15m. :thumbsup:
maria: Good. After rollout please run a full nightly on the 1000-prompt suite and file a postmortem. We should document this kernel ordering assumption in the runtime design doc and add the new regression test to CI. I'll open incident ticket INC-2024-031.
priya: Will also add telemetry to log per-segment prefetch/read timestamps for a week so we can see any edgecases.
zack: LGTM. Thanks for the quick triage everyone.
maria: Closing loop when prod confirms. :white_check_mark:
